name: AiSensy
tagline: A budget WhatsApp Business API platform claiming 150,000+ businesses on essentially bootstrapped funding — genuinely affordable, genuinely narrower than its omnichannel competitors.
tldr: AiSensy was founded in 2020 in Gurugram, India by Gautam Shelley, Mohit Dua, and Ajay Rathore, reporting total funding of only around $100K despite claiming 150,000+ businesses across 60+ countries and growing from ~7 employees in 2021 to 173 by 2026 — an unusually capital-efficient growth story if the figures hold up.

Pricing is genuinely low: Basic ₹1,500/month (~$18 USD) with unlimited users, Pro ₹3,200/month (~$38 USD) adding broadcast scheduling and campaign budgets — with WhatsApp's own per-conversation fees charged separately on top of either plan.

This is a WhatsApp-only platform, not a broader omnichannel tool — multi-agent live chat lets a team work from one shared WhatsApp number, but there's no native Instagram, Messenger, or other channel support documented.

The AI Chatbot is described in general terms (understanding customer needs, responding intelligently) without the specific technical detail — knowledge-base training method, resolution benchmarks — that some competitors document more precisely, and hands off to a human agent when it can't resolve a query.

Independent reviews are solid but a notch below direct competitors (4.3/5 on G2 versus roughly 4.6/5 for Wati and Gallabox), with specific, repeated complaints about basic campaign analytics, missing click-tracking, and pricing that one reviewer specifically calls unsuitable for startup businesses.

Best for small-to-mid Indian businesses wanting an affordable, no-frills WhatsApp Business API tool for support and broadcast marketing — not for teams needing broader channel coverage, deep analytics, or sophisticated AI resolution capability.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent Live Chat allowing a whole team to work from one shared WhatsApp Business number, with Live Chat Agent and Manager roles
A no-code AI Chatbot builder that responds to customer questions and notifies the team to take over when it can't resolve a query
Quick replies, saved responses, and internal notes for team coordination and faster responses
Scheduleable broadcast campaigns with smart audience segmentation for WhatsApp marketing
CTA-enabled notifications and click-through analytics for campaign performance tracking
Native integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, and HubSpot, available from the Basic plan
A separately-priced chatbot builder add-on (₹2,500/month) for teams wanting deeper conversational automation
AI Ads Manager and template generator tools bundled with higher-tier plans

faq.question: Does AiSensy support channels beyond WhatsApp?
faq.answer: No — this is a WhatsApp-only platform, unlike broader omnichannel competitors (Respond.io, Trengo, Wati) that also cover Instagram, Messenger, SMS, or voice. If your support and marketing volume is genuinely concentrated on WhatsApp specifically, that focus isn't a problem; if you need broader channel coverage, AiSensy isn't built for it.

faq.question: How much does AiSensy actually cost?
faq.answer: The published platform fee is genuinely low — ₹1,500/month (about $18 USD) for Basic with unlimited users, or ₹3,200/month (about $38 USD) for Pro. WhatsApp's own per-conversation fees are charged separately on top of either plan, and a chatbot builder add-on runs an additional ₹2,500/month if you want deeper conversational automation beyond the base plan.

faq.question: How sophisticated is AiSensy's AI chatbot?
faq.answer: It's described in fairly general marketing terms — using AI and machine learning to understand customer needs and respond intelligently — without the specific technical detail some competitors publish, such as a named knowledge-base training method or an independently-referenced resolution benchmark. It does document a real, functional handoff: when the chatbot can't resolve a query, it notifies the team so a human agent can take over.

faq.question: What's the most common complaint about AiSensy?
faq.answer: Analytics depth. Independent reviewers specifically describe campaign analytics as fairly basic, flag a lack of click-tracking in WhatsApp marketing campaigns as a real drawback, and generally note limitations in advanced analytics capabilities relative to competitors. One reviewer also specifically states the pricing isn't suitable for startup businesses, despite the relatively low headline platform fee.

faq.question: Does AiSensy integrate with Shopify?
faq.answer: Yes, and it's available starting from the Basic plan rather than gated to a higher tier — a genuinely accessible inclusion. WooCommerce and HubSpot integrations are also documented, though with less independently-confirmed depth of detail than the deeper, purpose-built Shopify-AI implementations some competitors (Wati, Interakt) offer.

faq.question: How does AiSensy compare to Wati or Gallabox?
faq.answer: AiSensy sits a notch below both on independent review scores (4.3/5 on G2 versus roughly 4.6/5 for Wati and Gallabox) and offers a narrower feature set — no independently confirmed deep AI-commerce integration comparable to Wati's Shopify cart-recovery app, and real reviewer complaints about analytics depth. Its clearest advantage is price: the published platform fees are meaningfully lower than most WhatsApp-focused competitors.

pricingBreakdown: AiSensy's headline platform fees are genuinely among the lowest in this comparison set — roughly $18/month for Basic and $38/month for Pro, both with unlimited users, which undercuts most competitors by a wide margin on the base subscription alone. The catch, consistent with every WhatsApp Business API platform in this category, is that WhatsApp's own per-conversation fees apply separately and aren't included in either number, and the chatbot builder add-on (₹2,500/month, roughly $30) is a further cost if you want deeper automation than the base plan includes. That said, at least one independent reviewer specifically describes the real total pricing as unsuitable for startup businesses — worth taking seriously even though it seems to contradict the low headline fee, since it likely reflects the combined weight of conversation fees and add-ons at real usage volume. Model your expected conversation volume against WhatsApp's own per-message rates before assuming the low platform fee represents your total monthly cost.

capabilities.note: AiSensy does one thing — WhatsApp Business API management — without trying to be a broader omnichannel platform. For a business whose support and marketing genuinely live entirely on WhatsApp, that focus keeps the product simple and the price low. For anyone needing Instagram, Messenger, or other channel coverage, this isn't the right tool at all.

verdict: AiSensy's growth story is genuinely notable on its own terms — reportedly scaling to 150,000+ businesses and 173 employees on roughly $100K in total funding is an unusually capital-efficient trajectory if the figures hold up, and it tracks with a product built to be simple and cheap rather than feature-maximal. The pricing reflects that philosophy directly: genuinely low platform fees with unlimited users, real Shopify and WooCommerce integration available from the entry tier, and straightforward multi-agent live chat that reviewers describe as easy to pick up. Where this product is honestly outmatched by its closest competitors is depth. It's WhatsApp-only, with no other channel to unify into a broader omnichannel view the way Respond.io, Trengo, or even Wati document. The AI chatbot is real but described in general terms without the specific technical grounding — named training methods, resolution benchmarks — that more AI-forward competitors publish, and independent reviewers consistently and specifically flag analytics depth and click-tracking as real gaps rather than a vague 'could be better' complaint. My honest read: if your business genuinely lives on WhatsApp alone, doesn't need sophisticated AI resolution or deep reporting, and wants the lowest realistic platform fee in this category, AiSensy does that specific job well. If you need broader channel coverage, deeper AI capability, or more mature analytics, look at Wati, Trengo, or Respond.io instead — all reviewed elsewhere on this site — even though they cost meaningfully more.
